mainTopic: A one-day-old baby's status (inheritance, the בכור's share, murder, mourning), and the age of three years and one day for a girl's relations to count legally
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why a one-day-old baby 'inherits and passes on inheritance': a living baby can inherit his mother and pass it to his paternal brothers, but an עובר is presumed to die before its mother. The גמרא challenges this with a case where a fetus twitched after the mother died, and מר בריה דרב אשי answers that this was like a lizard's severed tail. מר בריה דרב יוסף, quoting רבא, explains that the baby reduces the בכור's double share, while a son born after the father's death does not ('וילדו לו'); in פומבדיתא they taught that a בכור born after his father's death gets no double share ('יכיר'), and the הלכה follows all these versions. The גמרא then learns from 'כל נפש' that killing a one-day-old is murder, and רב פפא explains that his family mourns for him, in a case where we know the pregnancy was full term, which fits even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A new משנה rules that from three years and one day, relations with a girl count fully for קידושין, יבום, אשת איש, טומאה, תרומה, כהונה and עריות, and below that age they do not. A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר says three years, and the גמרא offers two explanations of the difference: the school of רבי ינאי (one day) and רבי יוחנן (thirty days counting as a year). The amud ends with a second ברייתא where רבי מאיר allows even two years and one day, challenging the school of רבי ינאי; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the rule: a son cannot inherit from his mother once he is in the grave
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the earlier explanation: a fetus does not inherit from its mother to pass the inheritance on to its paternal brothers, because a son does not inherit his mother while he is already in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A son does not inherit his mother while he is] in the grave, in order to pass it on to his brothers from the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started just before this section. It explains why an עובר does not inherit from its mother: it is assumed to have died first, and a dead son cannot inherit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living baby inherits his mother's property. When he dies, it passes to his paternal half-brothers. But a fetus is presumed to die before its mother, so it never inherits, and nothing passes through it to those brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: In the grave, meaning after the son has already died
To pass on an inheritance to one's own heirs
A fetus that has not yet been born

steps.confusionAlert: The 'brothers from the father' are half-brothers who share only the father. They would never inherit the mother directly. They can only get her property by inheriting it through the baby.

phrases.english: in the grave, to pass on to his brothers from the father.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before: a son can't inherit his mother if he died first and is already 'in the grave'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of נוחל ומנחיל begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus is presumed to die before its mother, so it does not inherit her and cannot pass her property to its paternal half-brothers.

steps.title: Challenge: a fetus was seen moving after its mother died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the assumption that the fetus always dies first, citing a real incident where it moved three times after the mother died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But there was an incident, and the fetus twitched up to three twitches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption from step 1 that the fetus dies before its mother. It points to a real case where the fetus seemed alive after the mother's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus moved after the mother died, it seems it outlived her. Then it should inherit from her and pass the property on. That would contradict the rule that a fetus never inherits from its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? The opening of a challenge
An actual incident that happened
A twitch or spasm, a jerking movement

phrases.english: Is that so?
But there was an incident,
and it twitched up to three twitches!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the fetus, moving after its mother had already died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the presumption stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The presumption that a fetus dies before its mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real case showed the fetus moving after the mother's death, which suggests it was still alive and outlived her.

steps.title: Answer: like a lizard's tail that twitches after being cut off
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב אשי explains that the movements were only reflex spasms, like a lizard's severed tail, not a sign of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרב אשי said: It is just like the tail of a lizard, which twitches.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרב אשי defends the rule. The movements of the fetus did not mean it was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lizard's tail keeps jerking after it is cut off, even though it is clearly not alive. In the same way, the fetus's twitches were only leftover motion. So the presumption that the fetus died first still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; introduces a comparison
The tail of a lizard

steps.whatToRemember: Twitching after death is not life. The fetus is still treated as dying before its mother, so it does not inherit from her.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Ashi, said:
It is just like the tail of a lizard, which twitches.
phrases.notes: He means a tail that has been cut off. It moves, but it isn't alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the evidence: the movement was a reflex, not life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fetus's twitches show it outlived its mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twitches were like a severed lizard tail's, so the fetus is still presumed dead first.

steps.title: A different explanation: the baby reduces the firstborn's portion
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב יוסף, quoting רבא, explains that the משנה means a one-day-old baby counts as a son and so lowers the בכור's double portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא: [The משנה comes] to say that he reduces the firstborn's portion.
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of the משנה's words 'נוחל ומנחיל' is offered. The point is that the baby counts as one of the father's sons when the inheritance is divided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור gets two shares, and each other son gets one. If there are two sons, the estate is split in three, and the בכור gets two-thirds. If a baby son also counts, the estate is split in four, and the בכור gets only half. So the baby 'reduces' the בכור's portion.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn son, who receives a double share
The firstborn's extra portion of the inheritance
Reduces, makes smaller

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
[It comes] to say that he reduces the firstborn's portion.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the one-day-old baby from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּמַעֵט בְּחֵלֶק בְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the משנה from the one completed in steps 1-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-day-old son counts among the heirs and reduces the firstborn's double portion.

steps.title: A son born after the father's death does not reduce the firstborn's portion
steps.stepSummary: Also in the name of רבא: a son born after the father died does not lower the בכור's share, because the פסוק says 'וילדו לו', born to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא: A son born after the father's death does not reduce the firstborn's portion. What is the reason? We require 'and they bore him [children]'.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרב יוסף adds a limit to the rule in step 4. Only a son born while the father was alive counts against the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's section on the בכור begins with 'וילדו לו', meaning sons born to the father. A son born after the father's death was not born to him in his lifetime. That is why the משנה speaks of a one-day-old baby and not a fetus: a fetus at the time of the father's death would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'And they bore him [children]', from the בכור section in the תורה
We require

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה picked a baby who was already born, and also sets a practical rule for dividing an estate.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: And Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
A son who was born after the father's death
does not reduce the firstborn's portion.
What is the reason?
We require 'and they bore him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: בֵּן שֶׁנּוֹלַד אַחַר מִיתַת הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 4 to sons born during the father's lifetime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A posthumously born son does not reduce the firstborn's double portion, because 'וילדו לו' requires birth in the father's lifetime.

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version: a posthumous בכור gets no double portion
steps.stepSummary: In סורא they taught the statement as above. In פומבדיתא they taught that a בכור born after his father's death does not take a double portion, because the father must 'יכיר', recognize him.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it this way; in פומבדיתא they taught it this way: מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא: A firstborn born after his father's death does not take a double portion. What is the reason? We require 'he shall recognize', and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a second version of מר בריה דרב יוסף's teaching. In this version the posthumous child is the בכור himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the father 'יכיר', shall recognize, the בכור by giving him a double portion. A father who died before the birth cannot recognize the child. So such a בכור loses his extra share. The סורא version spoke about a younger son reducing the בכור's share; the פומבדיתא version is about the בכור himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A double portion
'He shall recognize', the father's acknowledgment of the בכור
It is not there, it is missing

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of the same teacher: in סורא, a posthumous son does not reduce the בכור's share ('וילדו לו'). In פומבדיתא, a posthumous בכור does not get a double share ('יכיר').
steps.confusionAlert: These are not two different rabbis arguing. It is one statement of מר בריה דרב יוסף, remembered differently in two ישיבות.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught it this way,
in Pumbedita they taught it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא —
phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
A firstborn who was born after his father's death
does not take a double portion.
What is the reason?
We require 'he shall recognize,' and that is not there.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17. The father has died, so there is no one to recognize the בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי, בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the teaching in step 5, based on a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A firstborn born after his father's death does not receive a double portion, because the father must 'יכיר' (recognize) him.

steps.title: The הלכה follows all of רבא's statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows every version of what מר בריה דרב יוסף reported in the name of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like all these versions of the statements of מר בריה דרב יוסף in the name of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion about the בכור's double portion by giving a final ruling. Every statement brought in רבא's name is accepted as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three rulings were quoted: a one-day-old baby lowers the בכור's share; a son born after the father died does not lower it; and a בכור born after the father died does not get a double portion. The two versions from סורא and פומבדיתא do not conflict, so the גמרא accepts both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law; how we actually rule
Versions; different ways a teaching was passed down

steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's rulings about the בכור's portion are accepted as practical הלכה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with all these versions
phrases.notes: Both the version taught in סורא and the one taught in פומבדיתא, from the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: of Mar, son of Rav Yosef, in the name of Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the series of רבא statements in steps 4 to 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows all of רבא's rulings: a one-day-old lowers the בכור's share, a posthumous son does not, and a posthumous בכור gets no double portion.

steps.title: Killing a one-day-old baby makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one who kills a one-day-old is liable, and gives the source from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who kills him is liable. This is because it is written, 'And a man who strikes any person' (כל נפש), meaning any person at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה: one who kills a one-day-old baby is liable for murder. It shows where this comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כל נפש', any person, without limiting it. From the word 'כל' the גמרא learns that the law of murder applies in every case, even to a baby just one day old.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable; legally responsible for punishment
Any person; any living human being
In any case; no matter what

phrases.english: And one who kills him is liable.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, talking about a one-day-old baby.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And a man who strikes any person"
— meaning in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after finishing the inheritance discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing even a one-day-old baby is murder, learned from the word 'כל' in 'כל נפש'.

steps.title: What does counting like a full person mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying the baby counts like a full person for his relatives, and asks which law this is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and he is to his father, his mother and all his relatives like a full חתן. For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and asks what practical law it refers to. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a one-day-old is like a 'חתן שלם' for his family, but it does not say in which area of law. The גמרא wants to know exactly what difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a complete groom'; here, a fully grown person
His relatives
For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: And he is, to his father and to his mother
and to all his relatives, like a full groom.
phrases.notes: In other words, even though he is only a day old, his family treats him like a grown person.

phrases.english: For what law is this said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה and asks for its practical meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of הלכה the משנה means when it calls the baby a 'חתן שלם' for his relatives.

steps.title: It is about mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה is talking about אבלות: the family must mourn for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is about mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: the משנה means that the relatives must keep the laws of אבלות if this baby dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the baby a 'full person' means his death is treated like any adult's death. His father, mother and other relatives must mourn for him, even though he lived only one day.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning; the laws a relative keeps after a death
With regard to; concerning

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: With regard to mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to אבלות: relatives must mourn for a baby who dies at one day old.

steps.title: This seems to go against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that mourning for a one-day-old seems to contradict רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds that a baby under thirty days might be a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom is this? It is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said: any human who lived thirty days is not a נפל. That means if he did not live thirty days, he is in doubt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. It argues that it cannot fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is unsure whether a baby under thirty days was ever fully viable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that only after thirty days do we know a baby is not a נפל. So a one-day-old who dies is a doubt, and we would not be sure we must mourn for him. This seems to clash with the משנה's ruling that the family mourns.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
A baby born not fully viable, who was never going to live
A doubt; uncertain status

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not say every baby under thirty days is a נפל. He says such a baby is in doubt. Only after thirty days are we sure he is viable.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Like whom? Not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said: Any that lived thirty days
among humans is not a non-viable baby.
This implies that if he did not live that long, he is in doubt!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 10 by comparing it to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's thirty-day rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling, as explained by רב פפא, that relatives mourn for a one-day-old.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a baby under thirty days might be a נפל, so mourning would be uncertain. The משנה would then not fit his view.

steps.title: The case is a baby born after a full pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a baby whom we know was born after a full nine months, so even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees he is not a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where it is known that his months of pregnancy were complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The משנה is talking about a baby we know was born after a full pregnancy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's doubt only applies when we do not know whether the pregnancy was complete. If we know the baby was carried to full term, he is surely viable even before thirty days. So the משנה can fit everyone, including רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a ruling to a specific case
It is known to him; he is certain
His months of pregnancy were completed; he was carried to full term

steps.whatToRemember: A one-day-old counts as a full person for mourning when we know he was born after a full pregnancy. This fits even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's thirty-day rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the thirty-day rule is only a way to settle a doubt. When we already know the pregnancy was full, there is no doubt to settle.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where it is known that his months were completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? דְּקִים לֵיהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה deals only with a baby known to have been carried to full term.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to speak of any one-day-old, which would clash with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's doubt about babies under thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a baby known to be full term. Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees such a baby is viable, so the family mourns.

steps.title: From three years and one day, relations with a girl count fully
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a girl of three years and one day can become married through ביאה. A יבם acquires her through ביאה. Another man is liable for being with her as an אשת איש. If she is a נדה, she passes טומאה to the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A girl who is three years and one day old can be betrothed through relations. If her יבם has relations with her, he acquires her as his wife. A man who has relations with her while she is married is liable for being with an אשת איש. If she is a נדה, she makes the man impure, and he then makes the bedding under him impure, but only at the level of the top covering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that once a girl is three years and one day old, relations with her count as real relations for marriage, יבום, אשת איש and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is an age line: from three years and one day, the act counts legally. So it can create קידושין, it completes יבום, it makes another man guilty of אשת איש, and it passes נדה impurity to the man. The man's impurity reaches the bedding beneath him only at a lighter level, the same level as the top cover of a זב.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being discussed
She becomes betrothed through relations, one of the ways to make קידושין
The brother of a man who died without children, who may marry the widow
A married woman; being with her is a severe sin
The bedding underneath gets only the lighter impurity of the top covering

steps.confusionAlert: The lower bedding does not become a full source of impurity here. It only gets the weaker impurity that a cover on top of a זב gets.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A girl who is three years and one day old
can be betrothed through relations
and if a יבם has relations with her
he acquires her as his wife
and one is liable for her because of a married woman
and she makes impure the man who has relations with her
phrases.notes: This is talking about when she is a נדה.

phrases.english: so that he makes impure the bedding beneath him
like the upper covering
phrases.notes: The bedding under him only gets the lighter impurity, the same as the covering on top of a זב.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier steps were about a one-day-old boy, and this משנה moves to the age at which a girl's relations count legally.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From three years and one day, relations with a girl count fully for קידושין, יבום, אשת איש and נדה impurity.

steps.title: Further results: תרומה, disqualifying from כהונה, and עריות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the list. If she marries a כהן, she eats תרומה. If a פסול man has relations with her, she becomes unfit for כהונה. If a relative from the עריות has relations with her, he gets the death penalty, but she is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she marries a כהן, she may eat תרומה. If one of the men who are unfit for כהונה has relations with her, he makes her unfit for כהונה. If one of the עריות listed in the תורה has relations with her, those men are put to death because of her, and she is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing more areas of הלכה where relations with a girl of three years and one day count fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the act counts, it has both good and bad results. It can let her eat תרומה as a כהן's wife, and it can disqualify her from כהונה. Even a severe עריות punishment applies to the man. She is exempt because she is a minor and is not punished.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which his household may eat
Men unfit for כהונה, such as a ממזר or a חלל
He makes her unfit to marry a כהן
Forbidden relations listed in the תורה
She is exempt from punishment

phrases.english: If she marries a כהן
she may eat תרומה
if one of the unfit men has relations with her
phrases.notes: Men unfit for כהונה, such as a ממזר or a חלל.

phrases.english: he makes her unfit for כהונה
if one of all the forbidden relatives has relations with her
that are stated in the Torah
they are put to death because of her
and she is exempt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of rulings from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her relations count for eating תרומה, for being disqualified from כהונה, and for the man's death penalty in עריות, while she herself is exempt.

steps.title: Below that age the act does not count
steps.stepSummary: If the girl is younger than three years and one day, relations with her have no legal effect. The משנה compares it to putting a finger in an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is younger than that, it is like putting a finger into the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by giving the other side of the age line: if she is younger than three years and one day, none of the rulings above apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison means that the act leaves no lasting change. When a finger touches the eye, the eye tears and then goes back to how it was. In the same way, at this young age her body returns to its original state, so the act does not count as ביאה in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than that, meaning younger than three years and one day
Like putting a finger in the eye: something that leaves no lasting effect

steps.whatToRemember: Three years and one day is the age line. From then on, relations with a girl count fully for קידושין, יבום, אשת איש, טומאה, תרומה, כהונה and עריות. Before that age, the act has no legal effect.

phrases.english: Less than that
is like putting a finger into the eye
phrases.notes: The eye tears up but goes back to normal. So too here, nothing lasting happens, and the act does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the age line set in steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below three years and one day, relations with a girl carry no legal weight.

steps.title: A ברייתא: three years versus three years and one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר says a three-year-old girl can be betrothed through ביאה, and the חכמים require three years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: a girl of three years can be betrothed through ביאה. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say she must be three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting a ברייתא that shows the age in our משנה (three years and one day) is really a dispute. רבי מאיר gives a slightly younger age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said 'three years and one day,' which matches the חכמים in this ברייתא. רבי מאיר says just 'three years.' The gap between the two views looks tiny, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: She becomes betrothed (gets קידושין)
Through intercourse, which is one of the ways קידושין can be done
The Rabbis, the majority view that argues on רבי מאיר

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
A girl of three years is betrothed through intercourse,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
A girl of three years and one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that shows the age in the משנה is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: three years is enough. חכמים: three years and one day.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real difference is between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next move: what actual case would these two views decide differently?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree she cannot be betrothed before about three years. The difference between them seems to be only one day, so the גמרא wants to know exactly where their rulings split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for the practical case where two opinions disagree.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where רבי מאיר and the חכמים rule differently.

steps.title: The school of רבי ינאי: the difference is the last day of the third year
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says the only difference is the day before her fourth year begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: the difference between them is the eve of the new year.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the two views differ only on one day: the last day of her third year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On that day she has finished three full years, so רבי מאיר says she can be betrothed. The חכמים say she must reach the first day of her fourth year. Here the dispute is truly just one day.

keyTerms.meaning: The house or school of a sage
Here it means the eve of her new year, the last day before her fourth year begins
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Here עֶרֶב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה does not mean the day before the holiday of ראש השנה. It means the day before the girl's own fourth year begins.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
The eve of the new year is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means the last day of her third year, right before her fourth year starts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The only difference is the last day of the third year. רבי מאיר allows it on that day and the חכמים do not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: do thirty days count as a whole year?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the dispute is whether thirty days into a year count as a full year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is whether thirty days in a year count as a year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer to the question 'what is the difference between them.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר holds that thirty days into the third year count as the whole year. So a girl of two years and thirty days already counts as three. The חכמים disagree and require three years and one day, which makes the gap much bigger than one day.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirty days into a year are treated as a full year

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that thirty days in a year count as a year comes up in other places in the גמרא. Here רבי יוחנן uses it to explain רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whether thirty days in a year are considered a year
is the difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 17, different from רבי ינאי's school.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether thirty days in a year count as a year. רבי מאיר says yes, the חכמים say no.

steps.title: A challenge: רבי מאיר allows even two years and one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי's school with a ברייתא where רבי מאיר allows even a girl of two years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a girl of three years, and even of two years and one day, is betrothed through ביאה. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to attack the school of רבי ינאי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי מאיר allows a girl of two years and one day, almost a full year younger. So the dispute cannot be only about the last day of the third year, as רבי ינאי's school said.

keyTerms.meaning: And even. It adds a bigger case to the ruling.
Two years and one day, meaning just after her second birthday

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A girl of three years,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּת שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: and even a girl of two years and one day,
is betrothed through intercourse,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
A girl of three years and one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the explanation of רבי ינאי's school (step 18) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The school of רבי ינאי's claim that the dispute is only about the last day of the third year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר allows even two years and one day, so the gap between the views is far more than one day.
